key_insight: The CALPHAD-based Gamma metric correlates better with tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys than the DFT-based D-parameter, with comparable performance in compression.
engineering_relevance: Gamma could help screen refractory alloys for room-temperature ductility while targeting demanding high-temperature structural applications.
method: Combine the BCC–HCP free-energy difference with the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface.
Propose pairing Gamma with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility to address intrinsic and extrinsic ductility factors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a modest improvement in tensile-ductility correlation over the D-parameter and equally good compression performance, without quantitative evaluation details.
watch_item: Gamma alone does not capture oxygen-related embrittlement; its proposed coupling with oxygen solubility still requires validation.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
